newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian March export prices fall 1.4 pct.
newsitem.headline: Australian March export prices fall 1.4 pct.

text.p: Australian export prices fell 1.4 percent in March from the previous month and were 3.8 percent lower than a year earlier, the Australian Bureau of Statistics said on Thursday.
The bureau said the March fall in the export price index was mainly due to the appreciation of the Australian dollar against major trading currencies.
Coal and iron ore prices decreased in March due to the appreciation of the Australian dollar, and lower world market prices led to decreases in the prices of gold and wheat.
"Slightly ofsetting these decreases was an increase in the price of frozen beef, reflecting tight supply in overseas markets."
The index fell to 91.6 in March from 92.9 in February.
The March monthly fall follows two consecutive increases, with 10 decreases recorded in the last 14 months.
